title: OpenAI GPT-4b micro & Retro Biosciences Engineer Yamanaka Stem-Cell Factors with 50× Reprogramming Gains
whyItMatters: OpenAI’s biology-tuned GPT-4b micro redesigned the Nobel-winning Yamanaka reprogramming proteins (SOX2 and KLF4), achieving >50× higher pluripotency marker expression and improved DNA repair in wet-lab human cells.
summary: In August 2025, OpenAI and longevity biotech Retro Biosciences published experimental results from GPT-4b micro, a biology-specialized small language model trained on protein sequences, structural context, and protein-interaction data. Tasked with redesigning the notoriously disordered Yamanaka transcription factors SOX2 and KLF4—which have historically resisted rational mutagenesis—GPT-4b micro proposed extensive multi-mutation variants (RetroSOX and RetroKLF) that achieved over 50-fold increases in pluripotency marker expression and enhanced DNA-damage repair in wet-lab human fibroblast reprogramming assays across multiple donors.
technicalHighlights: Engineered RetroSOX and RetroKLF variants containing dozens of simultaneous mutations across intrinsically disordered regions where structure-only tools struggle.
Wet-lab assays demonstrated >50× gains in pluripotency marker expression alongside faster reprogramming kinetics and reduced DNA damage.
Validated across multiple human donor cell lines and reprogramming protocols in Retro Biosciences laboratories.
caveats: Disclosed via a joint OpenAI / Retro Biosciences technical report rather than a peer-reviewed journal publication; full sequence data, model weights, and independent academic replication remain limited.

scoreRationale.foundational: Shows that sequence-trained LLMs can substantially optimize intrinsically disordered transcription factors that evade traditional structure-based protein engineering.
scoreRationale.ripple: Higher-efficiency, lower-damage cellular reprogramming could accelerate induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) manufacturing and regenerative medicine.
scoreRationale.verification: Backed by multi-donor wet-lab validation at Retro Biosciences, but scored conservatively pending independent peer-reviewed journal publication and open replication.
scoreRationale.velocity: Proposed high-order multi-mutant variants far faster than iterative directed-evolution campaigns.
